advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _owner_lock_held return a tri-state, treating only ENOENT as 'no owner' and any other open/lock fault as 'unknown' (do not materialize as failed); open the probe O_RDONLY and create the lock file readable by other uids
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:127: fd = os.open(owner_lock_path(job_id, repo_root=repo_root), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:162: fd = os.open(owner_lock_path(job_id, repo_root=repo_root), os.O_RDWR)
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:163-164: except OSError: return False
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:168: return lock_kernel.is_contention(exc)  (ENOLCK/EIO etc. -> False)
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:378: if _inflight.is_job_active(job_id) or _owner_lock_held(job_id, repo_root): return False  -> falls through to stale -> _materialize_stale_running writes failed
src/rebar/_store/lock_kernel.py:188-189: non-contention errnos 'are real faults ... that must surface with their identity'
advisory.finding: _owner_lock_held fails open. Every os.open error (not just ENOENT) and every non-contention lock error returns False ('no live owner'). _running_record_is_stale then lets gate_status overwrite a live job's index with failed/daemon-stopped. The lock file is created with mode 0o600 and probed with O_RDWR, so a poller running as a different uid (common when blue/green containers run as different users) always gets EACCES and reproduces exactly the bug this change is meant to fix, with no sign that the probe never ran.
scenarios: New container runs as a different uid than the draining one: open(O_RDWR) on the 0o600 lock file raises EACCES, the job is reported failed, and a duplicate billable run starts
Shared volume without working lock support (ENOLCK): the probe errors, the job is treated as dead and its index overwritten
advisory.suggested_fix: Return False only for FileNotFoundError and for a successfully taken lock. For any other OSError or NoExclusiveLegError, log it and treat the job as not-stale (return True/'unknown') so the record is not overwritten. Open the probe with os.O_RDONLY (flock and LockFile work on read-only handles) and create the lock with a mode like 0o644 so pollers running as other uids can open it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Release the owner lock if record_gate_run/_spawn_gate_daemon raises before the daemon takes ownership of it
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:300: owner_lock = gate_runs.hold_owner_lock(handle.job_id)
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:310: _spawn_gate_daemon(handle, gate_type, ticket_id, work, owner_lock)
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:259: gate_runs.release_owner_lock(owner_lock, handle.job_id) is reached only inside the daemon's _bg finally
src/rebar/_opcert_binding.py:101-103: spawn_context_daemon starts a threading.Thread (start can raise)
advisory.finding: _start_gate_job takes the owner lock before record_gate_run/_spawn_gate_daemon without try/except. If spawning the daemon raises (e.g. RuntimeError 'can't start new thread' from Thread.start), the fd is never released. The lock stays held for the rest of the process's life, so pollers in every other process/container report the never-run job as 'running' forever instead of materializing it as failed after the grace window.
scenarios: Thread exhaustion makes spawn_context_daemon raise after the lock is taken and 'running' is recorded; cross-process gate_status never settles the job
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the record + spawn in try/except BaseException: call gate_runs.release_owner_lock(owner_lock, handle.job_id), then re-raise.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that asserts the owner lock is still held at the moment the terminal gate record is written
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:256-260: `rebar.llm.record_gate_run(record)` / `gate_runs.release_owner_lock(owner_lock, handle.job_id)` / `handle.complete(result=result, error=error)`, with the comment 'Release only after the terminal record: a poller that finds the lock free re-reads the record before declaring the job stranded.'

src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:378: `if _inflight.is_job_active(job_id) or _owner_lock_held(job_id, repo_root):`. Until handle.complete() runs, the in-process registry short-circuits, so the lock is never consulted during the test's polling.
tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py:1063: `assert not _lock_is_free(job_id)` is checked only while the job is running; 1070-1074 check 'passed' and a free lock only after completion.

Named violating input: swap src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py lines 256 and 259, so release_owner_lock runs before record_gate_run. The test still passes, yet a cross-process poller could see a free lock while the index still says 'running' and write failed/daemon-stopped. That is the duplicate-billable-run bug this change fixes.
advisory.finding: No test fails if the owner lock is released BEFORE the terminal record is written. The test named 'holds_the_owner_lock_until_the_terminal_record' only checks the lock while the job is running and after it has passed. In-process status polls are answered by the inflight registry, and handle.complete() runs after both lines, so the poll cannot see the ordering.
scenarios: A refactor moves release_owner_lock before record_gate_run, or into an earlier try block. Blue-green pollers again mark live jobs as daemon-stopped during the small window around completion, and the test suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the second test, monkeypatch rebar.llm.record_gate_run with a wrapper that, when called with a non-'running' status, records `_lock_is_free(rec['job_id'])` before delegating to the real function. After completion, assert the recorded value was False, meaning the lock was still held while the terminal record was written.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests where hold_owner_lock fails (open error / contention / NoExclusiveLegError) and assert the gate job still runs to a terminal record and the stale-running fallback still applies
evidence:
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py (added): `except OSError:
        logger.warning("gate_runs: could not open owner lock for %s" ...)
        return None` and `except (OSError, lock_kernel.NoExclusiveLegError): ... os.close(fd)
        return None`
Docstring contract (added): 'Best-effort: on failure the job still runs and pollers fall back to the registry rule.'
search_files for 'hold_owner_lock' under tests/ returned '(no matches)'; the new tests reach it only on the success path through review_plan_start.
advisory.finding: The best-effort failure paths added in hold_owner_lock (open fails, or the lock is already contended, so it returns None and closes the fd) and in _owner_lock_held (a non-contention OSError or NoExclusiveLegError returns False) have no tests. Nothing shows that a job whose lock could not be taken still runs and settles, or that release_owner_lock(None, ...) is a safe no-op.
scenarios: Named input: a review_plan_start call made while another process already holds `<job_id>.lock`. hold_owner_lock gets contention and should return None while the job still completes as 'passed'. A regression that raises or leaks the fd would not be caught.

Named input: lock_kernel.take_exclusive monkeypatched to raise NoExclusiveLegError (a platform with neither fcntl nor msvcrt). gate_run_status on a stale running record should still materialize failed/daemon-stopped through the registry fallback.
advisory.suggested_fix: Hold the lock from a helper subprocess (as in the first test) and call gate_runs.hold_owner_lock(job_id); assert it returns None. Then monkeypatch lock_kernel.take_exclusive to raise NoExclusiveLegError and assert gate_run_status on a stale running record returns status 'failed' with verdict 'daemon-stopped'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound owner-lock liveness by the same max-age ceiling as the inflight registry (e.g. treat a held lock on a record older than _MAX_AGE_SECONDS as stale), so a wedged leader still becomes failed/daemon-stopped.
evidence: Primary failure: the leader's daemon is stuck inside work(). The lock fd is released only in _bg's finally after work() returns (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:240-259: `result = work()` ... `gate_runs.release_owner_lock(owner_lock, handle.job_id)`).

Existing reclaim: src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:21-23 '# Reclaim only leaders that missed completion cleanup; 40 minutes is twice the normal gate window' `_MAX_AGE_SECONDS: float = 40 * 60`. src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:144-149 _sweep_locked pops entries older than that, and it runs on registration (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:168).

Old disposition: once the entry was swept, `_inflight.is_job_active(job_id)` was False, so _running_record_is_stale returned True and _materialize_stale_running wrote `"status": "failed", "verdict": "daemon-stopped"` (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:394-403). Polling callers got a terminal failure and could re-start the gate.

New disposition: src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:378 `if _inflight.is_job_active(job_id) or _owner_lock_held(job_id, repo_root): return False`. The wedged daemon's process still holds the flock, so _owner_lock_held returns True (is_contention), and gate_run_status returns status 'running' forever (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:433-435).
Affected caller: gate_status pollers branch on status running vs failed. They now keep polling a dead job instead of getting the terminal failure that tells them to re-run.
advisory.finding: The owner lock ignores the registry's max-age reclaim. A leader stuck in work() keeps the lock until its process exits, so gate_run_status never reaches the stale → failed/daemon-stopped path, even after the inflight registry has swept the wedged entry. Before the change, a poll after the sweep returned status 'failed' / verdict 'daemon-stopped'. Now it returns status 'running' indefinitely.
scenarios: An LLM call inside work() hangs with no timeout. After 40 minutes the registry sweep evicts the leader, but the fd stays open, so every poll (same container or the new blue-green container) reports 'running' with no end.
A new start with the same dedup key launches a fresh run after the sweep, but any client still holding the original job_id never sees it fail.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _running_record_is_stale, honor _owner_lock_held only while `time.time() - started_at` is under the inflight max-age ceiling (40 min / REBAR_GATE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS). Past that, fall through to the stale rule, as the registry sweep already does.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Release the owner lock (release_owner_lock) if record_gate_run or _spawn_gate_daemon raises after hold_owner_lock in _start_gate_job.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:300 `owner_lock = gate_runs.hold_owner_lock(handle.job_id)` is followed by record_gate_run 'running' (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:301-309) and `_spawn_gate_daemon(handle, gate_type, ticket_id, work, owner_lock)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:310), with no try/finally around them.
The only release is inside _bg's finally (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:259). If `spawn_context_daemon(_bg, ...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:264) raises, _bg never runs and the fd is never closed.

Old disposition: with no daemon running, a poll from another process, or from this one after the registry sweep (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:144-149), found the record stale and surfaced status 'failed' / verdict 'daemon-stopped' (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:394-403).
New disposition: the leaked fd keeps the flock held, so _owner_lock_held returns True (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:378) and gate_run_status reports 'running' until the MCP process exits.
advisory.finding: _start_gate_job takes the owner lock before record_gate_run and _spawn_gate_daemon, and nothing releases it if those calls raise. If spawn_context_daemon raises (for example 'can't start new thread'), the fd leaks and the lock stays held for the life of the process. The 'running' record that was already written can then never be materialized as failed/daemon-stopped, in any process.
scenarios: The thread limit is hit during a burst of gate starts. The start raises, but the job_id's index says running, and the leaked lock makes every poller believe the run is live.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the record/spawn calls in try/except BaseException: call gate_runs.release_owner_lock(owner_lock, handle.job_id), then re-raise. Ideally also write a terminal failed record and complete the handle.
